hook_text: Lost your phone, no compass, and you need to find north? Look down at your feet at lunchtime.
clip_script: Here in South Africa we live south of the tropics, so at midday the sun is always in the northern part of the sky. That means your shadow points south. Turn around and you are facing north. Want another clue? Look at the satellite dishes on the roofs. Every single one in the street points the same way, towards satellites hanging high above the equator, which is north of us. Once you have north, every other direction falls into place: east on your right, west on your left. And that is how geographers draw a sketch map of a neighbourhood: north arrow first, then the school, the shop, the clinic, and the directions between them. No phone required.
visual_style: A whiteboard learner standing at noon with a long shadow pointing south, a row of satellite dishes all tilting north, then a compass rose drawn on the ground.
pacing: Quick hook, two surprising clues, a satisfying compass reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and map your own neighbourhood.
